newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks seen opening mixed to higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks seen opening mixed to higher.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open mixed to higher in narrow trading on Tuesday, as Wall Street became more convinced the Republican party would keep its slim margin of control in Congress.
"It's still a watchful, waiting situation like yesterday," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "In the afternoon, the three-year note auction could impact bonds."
Standard & Poor's December futures rose 0.9 to 712.15 ahead of the opening and the long bond rose 12/32 to yield 6.63 percent.

"We should have a mixed to higher opening and it should be similar to yesterday's session, with the Dow bouncing back and forth across the plus or minus level," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.
On Monday, the Dow industrials rose 20 to close at about 6042, but the Nasdaq Composite slipped one to about 1221.
Brown said the market performed well because investors are less worried that Democratics would win control of Congress in Tuesday's presidential and congressional elections.
"If they get a surprise tonight, tomorrow could be a bad day."
The first leg of the U.S. Treasury's three-part quarterly refunding auctions begins later in the day. The Treasury will offer $18.5 billion worth of three-year notes.
